name: Dialetto di Guardia Piemontese / Guardiolo
confidence_why: No source states where Gardiol word stress falls: Morosi 1890 only lists accent-marked words (réiç, pjęna, maǵénᵘ, litikkᵘ) and imperative-plus-clitic pairs, and Micali 2016 adds only that imperative groups with enclitics stress the last element, so the record stays undetermined and any placement rule would be a guess.

new_statements.quote: Accento. 158. réiç, méur; aiᵉr jeri, cfr. nm. 7; pieṅ all. al femin. pjęna; e ancora v. i nm. 30 32 37. — 159. lóurᵘ nm. 156. — 160. bęuka-mé guardami, cóǵǵi-té còricati, višť-lǔ vèstilo; all. a bęuké-me guardàtemi, aǵǵüé-me ajutatemi, višté-lu vestitelo. — 161. s'mèṅᵘ, pöṅǵénᵘ pettino, maǵénᵘ màcino; męrittᵘ, litikkᵘ, pęrdikkᵘ, vumbikkᵘ vomito, nivikka, pićikkᵘ appiccico.
new_statements.translation: Accent. 158. [retracted accent:] réiç, méur; aiᵉr 'yesterday', cf. no. 7; pieṅ beside the fem. pjęna; and see further nos. 30, 32, 37. — 159. [advanced accent:] lóurᵘ, no. 156. — 160. bęuka-mé 'look at me', cóǵǵi-té 'lie down', višť-lǔ 'dress him'; beside bęuké-me 'look (pl.) at me', aǵǵüé-me 'help (pl.) me', višté-lu 'dress (pl.) him'. — 161. [foreign accent:] s'mèṅᵘ, pöṅǵénᵘ 'I comb', maǵénᵘ 'I grind'; męrittᵘ, litikkᵘ, pęrdikkᵘ, vumbikkᵘ 'I vomit', nivikka 'it snows', pićikkᵘ 'I stick'.

The reader's quote matches word for word; differences are only in diacritic approxima…
new_statements.rule_in_words: No opened source states a general rule. Morosi's 'Accento' paragraph, in the AGI Neogrammarian format, lists only departures from the inherited (Latin/Romance) stress: retracted and advanced accent in a few words, stress moved onto the enclitic in singular imperative + clitic (bęuka-mé) versus plural imperatives stressed on the verb ending (bęuké-me), and Italian/Calabrian antepenult-stressed verbs re-stressed on the penult (pöṅǵénᵘ 'pettino', vumbikkᵘ 'vomito'); §190b adds that old proparoxytone infinitives survive only syncopated (strenr, najs'r). Read together with the parallel Pral section ('Accento mutato, per intolleranza dello sdrucciolo', §193) the data imply stress confined to the last two syllables (penult before a final schwa/-a, final in consonant-final words), i.e. the ordinary Occitan pattern with proparoxytones eliminated — but this is an inference from word lists, not a statement.
new_statements.exceptions: Morosi: retracted accent in réiç, méur, aiᵉr, pieṅ (§158), advanced accent in lóurᵘ (§159), imperative+enclitic stress on the clitic (§160), 'foreign' (Italian/Calabrian) proparoxytones adapted to penult stress (§161). Micali 2016 fn. 40 (p. 195): 'In guardiolo i costrutti imperativi con enclisi presentano accento sull'ultimo elemento come in generale nei dialetti occitani'.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level, isolated lexical items in Morosi's phonetic notes (informants: P. Molinari, A. Starnile, and two soldiers Muglia and Martillotti interviewed in Brescia, 1888); the only explicit stress remark concerns imperative + enclitic groups.
new_statements.identity_note: Gardiol = the Vivaro-Alpine Occitan of the Waldensian colony of Guardia Piemontese (Cosenza), Glottolog gard1245 (no ISO code; Glottolog files Kunert's grammar and dictionary under Occitan [oci]). Morosi 1890 describes exactly this variety ('dialetto di Guardia Piemontese in Calabria Citeriore') as an appendix to his description of the Piedmontese Waldensian dialects (Pral etc., different languoids); the earlier scan's 'not found online' was wrong — the appendix is in AGI vol. XI (1890), pp. 381-393, on archive.org (Micali's bibliographies cite it as vol. XII, but the scan's title page reads 'Volume undecimo, 1890').

No general sentence on where stress fall…
